user.title: Layered light
user.description: Layers for a real light, each a light of its own: <light>_base, the normal state (point schedules and scenes at it), and the layers above it. The real light shows the highest layer that is on. Changes made at the real light itself (its switch, the app, "all lights off") become the base and turn the layers off. More layers later under Options.

data_description.name: Empty: the real light's name.
data_description.layer: Optional, e.g. Door: a layer with priority 10.
data_description.wall_switch: Smart bulb behind an ordinary switch: when it comes back on after being unreachable, someone switched it on there, so that becomes the normal state.

error.layered: That is a layer; pick the real light.

add_layer.title: Add a layer
add_layer.description: A light of its own above the base. While it is on, the real light shows it (the highest priority wins); off, it lets the layers below through.

data_description.wall_switch: Smart bulb behind an ordinary switch: when it comes back on after being unreachable, someone switched it on there, so that becomes the normal state.

error.duplicate: There already is a layer with that name.

turn_on.name: Turn on (base layer)
turn_on.description: Turns lights on. A real light with layers is switched through its base layer, so the layers above it stay as they are; other lights as with the light action. Takes areas, devices and labels too (they name the real lights; the layers are hidden). Further fields of the light action are passed on.
